security_audit.summary: Most static command and URL findings are Markdown examples or documentation links, not hidden execution or data transfer. Real risk remains in the self-hosted cache sample, which uses user-derived filesystem paths without authentication, and in cache inputs that include environment files. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Self-hosted remote cache sample lacks production safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Add token authentication, per-team authorization, canonical path validation, artifact size limits, safe storage boundaries, and enabled cache signatures.

remediation.issue: Environment files are included as global cache dependencies.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify when .env files may be hashed, warn about secrets in .env.local, and prefer explicit non-secret inputs when possible.

createReadStream is called on filePath built from route and query parameters without authentication or canonical path validation. This can expose cache artifacts or unintended files if copied into a service.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure Self-Hosted Cache Example
semantic_findings.description: The Express cache server builds paths from teamId and hash values, accepts unauthenticated uploads, and disables remote cache signatures. A copied deployment could allow cache poisoning, unsafe writes, and artifact reads outside the intended team scope.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly joins user-controlled route and query values into filesystem paths, writes request bodies, and sets signature to false. The example also passes a token in the client command, but the server does not validate it.

content.value_statement: Monorepo builds can waste time when cache inputs and outputs are unclear. This skill provides Turborepo templates for caching, CI filters, remote cache setup, and cache debugging.
actual_capabilities: Defines turbo.json tasks with dependsOn, inputs, outputs, env, cache, and persistent settings.
Shows Vercel remote cache setup for local development and CI builds.
Provides a GitHub Actions workflow using Turborepo filters and cache credentials.
Includes a self-hosted remote cache example using Express and artifact routes.
Lists cache debugging commands for dry runs, graphs, forced builds, and summaries.
Documents package filters for workspaces, dependencies, dependents, and changed packages.
limitations: Examples require review before production use, especially the self-hosted cache server.
It does not install Turborepo or verify commands inside your repository.
It does not cover every package manager or every Turborepo version.
It does not replace secrets management or CI security review.

use_cases.title: Speed Up CI Builds
use_cases.description: Create Turborepo pipeline settings and CI filters that build only affected packages while sharing cache results.

use_cases.title: Standardize Monorepo Tasks
use_cases.description: Define build, test, lint, typecheck, dev, and deploy tasks with clear inputs and outputs.

use_cases.title: Investigate Cache Misses
use_cases.description: Use debugging commands and configuration checks to explain why tasks do not reuse cached outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Cache Config
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new monorepo.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my monorepo package scripts and draft a Turborepo configuration for build, test, lint, typecheck, and dev tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Add Remote Cache to CI
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my GitHub Actions workflow to use Turborepo remote caching with CI secrets for the token and team.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Cache Misses
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these Turborepo logs and explain why build tasks miss the cache. Recommend input, output, and environment changes.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Cache Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this self-hosted Turborepo cache design for authentication, path validation, signature settings, and artifact storage controls.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks for a first Turborepo cache setup for web, docs, and shared packages.
output_examples.output: A task plan covering build dependencies, cached outputs, uncached dev tasks, environment inputs, and package filter usage.

output_examples.input: A CI owner wants to reduce pull request build time with remote caching.
output_examples.output: A workflow summary that stores cache credentials in CI secrets, installs dependencies, and runs filtered build and test tasks.

output_examples.input: A platform engineer reports repeated cache misses after small documentation changes.
output_examples.output: A diagnosis that compares task inputs, excluded file patterns, output directories, and environment variables that affect cache keys.

best_practices: Review cache inputs and outputs with dry runs before enabling remote cache.
Keep secrets out of cached outputs and use CI secrets for remote cache tokens.
Use filters in CI only after package dependency relationships are correctly declared.
anti_patterns: Copying the self-hosted cache example into production without authentication and path validation.
Caching dev servers or deployment tasks that should run every time.
Adding broad environment files without checking whether they contain secrets.

faq.question: What does this skill help configure?
faq.answer: It helps configure Turborepo tasks, cache inputs, outputs, remote caching, CI filters, and cache debugging workflows.

faq.question: Can it set up Vercel remote caching?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes local login, project linking, CI token variables, and filtered build examples.

faq.question: Does it support self-hosted remote caching?
faq.answer: It includes an Express example, but that example needs authentication, validation, and signature hardening before production use.

faq.question: Will it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and configuration examples that should be reviewed before use in a repository.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use CI secret storage for tokens and avoid placing secret values in cached outputs or broad cache inputs.

faq.question: Who benefits most from this skill?
faq.answer: Platform engineers, DevOps engineers, and monorepo maintainers who manage build speed and cache reliability benefit most.
